extracted.intended_audience: Prospective offerors/applicants responding to the ONR BAA (contractors, universities, non-profits, and subcontractors)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation/administrative criteria for preparing and submitting full proposals under the Office of Naval Research (ONR) BAA, including certifications, reporting, formatting, COI mitigation, and post-award obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) reporting (2 CFR Part 170)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any company, non-profit agency or university that applies for financial assistance (grants, cooperative agreements or TIAs) as either a prime or sub-recipient under this BAA must provide information in its proposal that describes the necessary processes and systems in place to comply with the reporting requirements identified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A. Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 2 CFR Part 170, including Appendix A, for detailed explanation of requirements, exceptions, and exemptions. Provide proposal-level description of processes/systems to comply with subaward and executive compensation reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certification (Federal Assistance Certifications Report)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Assistance Certifications Report is an attestation that the entity will abide by the requirements of various laws and regulations and the supplemental at Section F.2.iv above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As applicable, submit documentation such as SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobby Activities, and disclose any unpaid delinquent tax liability or felony conviction under any Federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Restrictions on Lobbying (applicants > $100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants, cooperative agreement awards, and TIA awards greater than $100,000 require certification of compliance with national policy concerning lobbying. Grant applicants shall provide this certification via SF424 (R&R) (Block 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification includes: (1) No Federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid to influence Federal award decisions; (2) If other funds were or will be paid for such influencing, complete and submit Standard Form-LLL; (3) Language of this certification must be included in award documents for all subawards at all tiers. Submission is a prerequisite under 31 U.S.C. 1352; failure to file may incur civil penalties of $10,000–$100,000 per failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding prohibition on internal confidentiality agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) block 17, the applicant certifies it does not require employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements that prohibit reporting to authorized Federal investigative or law enforcement representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification language is a material representation; false statements may subject signatory to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (18 U.S.C. § 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding disclosure of funding sources (Section 223(a), NDAA FY2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF 424 (R&R) Block 17 the proposing entity certifies compliance with Section 223(a) requiring that the PI and other key personnel certify current and pending support is current, accurate and complete; agree to update disclosures upon agency request prior to award and during term; and that PI/key personnel are aware of these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False or fraudulent statements may result in penalties under 18 U.S.C. §1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest - general disclosure requirement (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with codes of conduct to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in award and administration of contracts (2 CFR 200.318(c)). Offerors must disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest for themselves and any identified subrecipient included in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government may request additional information or require a conflict of interest mitigation plan subject to approval. Nondisclosure or misrepresentation may lead to disqualification or termination and other remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific conflict of interest disclosure (collaborations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific collaborations that arose from close collaboration prior to submission should be disclosed and considered potential conflicts of interest. Collaborators must be included in the list of current and pending support for senior and key researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all collaborators in current and pending support even if they did not formally provide support; disclosure mitigates perceived conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review use and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals funded as basic research, ONR may utilize peer reviewers from academia, industry, and Government to assist in periodic appraisal of performance under awards (ONR Instruction 3966.1A). Non-U.S. Government peer reviewers must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving proposal/report copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviews monitor quality and help determine continuation of funding. Offerors may include PI travel costs to attend peer review. Reviews may consider information from project/program review meetings (see BAA Section F.2.a.viii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain telecommunications and video surveillance equipment/services (Section 889 / 2 CFR 200.216 / 200.471)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and subrecipients are prohibited from obligating or expending loan or grant funds to procure, extend/renew contracts for, or enter contracts to procure equipment, services, or systems that use covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial/essential component or critical technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered equipment examples: Huawei, ZTE (telecom); Hytera, Hangzhou Hikvision, Dahua (video surveillance). Also covers equipment/services from entities the Secretary of Defense reasonably believes are owned/controlled by or connected to a covered foreign country (defined as the People’s Republic of China). See Public Law 115-232, section 889 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency assistance to transition from covered telecom/surveillance equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Heads of executive agencies administering loan, grant, or subsidy programs shall prioritize available funding and technical support to assist affected entities in transitioning from covered communications equipment and services to replacements and to sustain communications service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation may include prioritized funding and technical support to affected businesses and institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters reporting (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any Federal award may include more than $500,000 over the period of performance, the post-award reporting requirements (Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters) are applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ONR Addendum to DoD R&D General Terms and Conditions and Programmatic Requirements for post-award reporting guidance (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting threshold for active awards requiring SAM/FAPIIS information (>$10,000,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total value of your currently active grants, cooperative agreements, and procurement contracts from all Federal awarding agencies exceeds $10,000,000 for any period of time during the period of performance of this Federal award, you must maintain currency of information reported to SAM that is made available in the designated integrity and performance system (currently FAPIIS) about civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings described in the award term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is statutory under 41 U.S.C. 2313. Information posted (except past performance reviews for procurement) will be publicly available. Maintain and update SAM/FAPIIS information as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings required to be reported to SAM/FAPIIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Report proceedings that: (a) are connected with the award/performance of a Federal award; (b) reached final disposition during the most recent five-year period; and (c) are one of: (i) a criminal proceeding resulting in a conviction; (ii) a civil proceeding resulting in a finding of fault and payment of a monetary fine/penalty/restitution/damages of $5,000 or more; (iii) an administrative proceeding resulting in a finding of fault and payment of either a monetary fine/penalty of $5,000+ or reimbursement/restitution/damages in excess of $100,000; or (iv) any other proceeding that could have led to such outcomes or had a consent/compromise with acknowledgment of fault, provided disclosure does not conflict with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the definitions in the award term for 'administrative proceeding' and 'conviction' when determining reportability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for submitting proceedings information
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter required information about each reportable proceeding in the SAM Entity Management area. Do not resubmit information already provided via SAM for procurement contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SAM's required fields and formats when entering proceedings information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting frequency for proceedings information
rubrics_metrics.description: While subject to the requirement, you must report proceedings information through SAM for the most recent five-year period either to report new proceedings or affirm there is no new information. Recipients with cumulative Federal awards > $10,000,000 must disclose semiannually any information about criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain semiannual updates when cumulative awards exceed the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to Recipient Integrity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative proceeding: non-judicial adjudicatory process to determine fault/liability (e.g., SEC administrative proceedings, CBCA, ASBCA) in connection with Federal contract/grant performance. Conviction: judgment of criminal offense by a court, including nolo contendere. Total value of active awards: includes only Federal share and expected funding increments/options even if not exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine what to report and how to compute thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal package required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal package must include: (1) Cover page (PDF); (2) Proposal Checklist (PDF); (3) Technical Proposal Template (Word); (4) Cost Proposal Template (Excel) for prime and all proposed subcontractors; (5) DCAA Pre-award Survey of Prospective Contractor Accounting System Checklist (PDF) for contractors without an approved accounting system; (6) Statement of Work (Word); (7) ONR Contract Specific Representations and Certifications (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items 1–6 are located at the ONR website link provided. Instructions are embedded in templates. FedConnect will not accept a proposal unless the Cover Sheet is included. Proposal Checklist and Cost Proposal Template require completion of cost-related information. Attachments may be incorporated into the Proposal Checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal and attachment format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Format requirements for attachments: Paper Size 8.5 x 11 inches; Margins 1 inch; Spacing single or double-spaced; Font Times New Roman, 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these formatting rules across proposal documents and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of technical data/software with restrictions (intellectual property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must submit a separate list of all technical data or computer software that will be furnished to the Government with other than unlimited rights with the proposal checklist. The Government will assume unlimited rights if offerors fail to identify any intellectual property restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all proprietary claims to results, prototypes, and/or deliverables. If no restrictions are intended, state 'NONE.' If subcontract information is proprietary, it may be submitted via email to the Program Officer with identifying details.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and secure PDF guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents except the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet and Statement of Work Template must be submitted in a secure, pdf-compatible format. The Cost Proposal Spreadsheet must be in Microsoft Excel compatible format and the Statement of Work in Microsoft Word format. All attachments to required proposal documents must be secure, pdf-compatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure pdf-compatible format prevents unauthorized editing; a password should not be required to open the document. Amended proposals should be submitted following the same guidance as original proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option pricing and task-level cost breakdown requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed options identified but not fully priced out in the Cost Proposal Spreadsheet will not be included in any resulting contract. Options must be separately priced and separate spreadsheets provided for base period and each option. Provide a summary by period of performance and a breakdown of cost for each task in the Statement of Work. Sum of all costs by task worksheets must equal the total cost summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to separately price options will exclude them from award. Ensure cost spreadsheet consistency across sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Proposal Spreadsheet condition ('useable condition')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Excel spreadsheet should be in a 'useable condition' to aid Government evaluation. 'Useable condition' means the spreadsheet should visibly include and separately identify within each appropriate cell any/all inputs, formulas, calculations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide 'value only spreadsheets' (hard copy-style). Ensure cells show formulas and inputs to allow Government reviewers to validate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DCAA Pre-award Survey submission for contractors without approved accounting system
rubrics_metrics.description: DCAA Pre-award Survey of Prospective Contractor Accounting System Checklist must be submitted by contractors that do not have an approved accounting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the checklist (PDF) in the proposal package as item (5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed fee guidance and Contract Risk Factor considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed Fees on ONR Contracts: Government objective set per DFARS 215.404-71. The table provides ranges and normal values by Contract Risk Factor and Contract Type (Firm Fixed Price, Cost Plus Fixed Fee), and weights for Technical and Management/Cost Control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign weights to elements according to input to total performance risk (weights sum to 100%). Technology Incentive (TI) is rarely used at ONR; any consideration of TI requires strong justification and is subject to negotiation. Typical fee range for ONR contracts: 5% to 7.5%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission portals and registration (FedConnect / SAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR uses FedConnect for submission of full proposals for contracts and other transaction agreements. To use FedConnect, register with SAM (https://www.sam.gov/SAM/) and create a FedConnect account. If first in organization to register in FedConnect, SAM Marketing Partner ID (SAM MPIN) is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FedConnect how-to guide and support contacts are provided. Do not use the FedConnect Message Center to submit questions; email POCs in Section G for inquiries. MCWL topics require electronic submission via specified email addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient qualifications and responsibility determination (FAR 9.104-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts shall be awarded to responsible prospective contractors only. See FAR 9.104-1 for general standards for assessing responsibility. Applicants are requested to provide information with proposal submission to assist the Contracting Officer’s evaluation of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparency and documentation supporting responsibility (e.g., past performance, systems, disclosures) to assist the Contracting Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS review prior to award
rubrics_metrics.description: FAPIIS (Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System) will be checked prior to making an award. The information in FAPIIS will be used to judge the entity's integrity, business ethics, and record of performance under Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may comment in FAPIIS on information entered by Federal officials. The Contracting Officer will consider FAPIIS entries in responsibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Property / Government Furnished Equipment and Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Government research facilities and operational military units are available and should be considered as potential government-furnished equipment/facilities. Offerors should indicate in the Proposal Checklist which of these facilities are critical for the project's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use and negotiation of GFE/GFF will occur as program unfolds. These facilities are of high value and in demand; include justification for criticality in Proposal Checklist, Section II, Block 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Arms, Ammunition, and Explosives (A&E) – safety and security requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors proposing to utilize ammunition and/or explosives (A&E) must comply with DoD Manual 4145.26-M (DoD Contractor’s Safety Manual for Ammunition and Explosives) and related DFARS clauses (e.g., 252.223-7002, 252.223-7003, 252.223-7007). A preaward safety survey (SF 1403) is required if A&E will be used. For Government-provided A&E containing nitrocellulose-based propellants or nitrate esters, NMCARS 5252.223-9000 also applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sensitive AA&E (Security Risk Category I–IV) are to be used, a preaward security survey is required and Contracting Officer will prepare SF 1403. The Government may require perimeter fencing, and the Offeror must provide AA&E accountability procedures; include procedures with proposal as required. See DoD 5100.76-M for security requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) clauses incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.204-7 (System for Award Management) and FAR 52.204-13 (System for Award Management Maintenance) are incorporated into this BAA; FAR 52.204-13 will be incorporated in all awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SAM registration and maintenance of accurate SAM information as clauses will be applied to awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment Eligibility Verification (E-Verify) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of FAR-based procurement contracts must enroll as Federal Contractors in E-Verify and use E-Verify to verify employment eligibility of all employees assigned to the award. All resultant contracts will include FAR 52.222-54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and use E-Verify for employees working on the contract as required by FAR provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) disclosure and required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors shall state in their proposal whether they are aware of any information bearing on the existence of any actual or potential OCI as defined in FAR 2.101 and FAR Subpart 9.5 for themselves and proposed subcontractors/partners/consultants/affiliates. Offerors performing SETA for ONR are considered to have an OCI that may not be susceptible to mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no OCI exists, include a certification statement: 'I [NAME] ... certify that NO actual or potential organizational conflict of interest (OCI) exists...' If OCI exists or offeror provides support services to ONR, submit: (i) name of entity supported, (ii) contract number(s), (iii) concise description of OCI facts, (iv) a Mitigation Plan, and (v) concluding certification statement. Nondisclosure or misrepresentation may disqualify offeror or lead to termination/default and other remedies under 18 U.S.C. §1001 and 31 U.S.C. §3802(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan minimum contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Mitigation Plan must, at a minimum: (i) provide organizational charts showing structure as related to performance and relevant contracts/agreements, highlighting elements creating the OCI; (ii) demonstrate how elements creating OCI will be isolated from resources that will perform the work; (iii) show whether performing organizational elements will be geographically or physically separated from elements creating the OCI; (iv) describe personnel reassignment processes for each relevant contract/agreement, including restrictions; (v) describe controls, including nondisclosure agreements, over future employment of departing employees as it relates to the OCI; (vi) describe any OCI training offered/required for employees (timing, frequency, length, content); (vii) provide evidence of facts and circumstances asserted to mitigate/address OCI concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should refer to FAR Subpart 9.5 for policies/procedures. The Contracting Officer will review the Mitigation Plan and may require additional information. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review outcomes and remedies for OCI
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer may: (1) impose conditions to avoid the conflict, (2) disqualify the offeror, (3) determine award in Government's best interest with appropriate mitigation conditions included, or (4) seek a waiver. If an actual or significant potential OCI exists that cannot be reasonably avoided, neutralized, or mitigated, the offeror will be ineligible for award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose required information or make required certifications concerning OCI will result in disqualification from award consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative FAR/DFARS/NMCARS provisions and clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation lists example FAR/DFARS/NMCARS provisions and clauses that may be applicable to ONR contracts; ONR reserves the right to include any relevant and current clauses necessary in the final award based on award dollar value.
